lines.text: Build, then review, then test. The pipeline exists, but only in your head, and in a few scattered settings.
So nobody else can see it, and when something breaks, nobody knows which stage to blame.
Workflows turn the pipeline into a visual graph, where every stage is a node you can see.
Each workspace is a stage. The build workspace, the review workspace, and the test workspace each get a place.
Events connect them. When build finishes, it emits code changed, and the next stage listens for it.
Drag a workspace onto an event, and an event onto a workspace. No config files, no glue code.
As you connect the pieces, the graph draws itself, so you always see the shape of the whole.
Then watch it run. Each event fires, and each workspace picks up its next task.
Every handoff shows up on the timeline, so you see what fired what, and when.
Each workspace keeps its approvals, so a chain never skips a human on a risky step.
Save the graph as a named workflow, and the whole team shares the same picture.
